what: The catalog's vocabulary as the database currently holds it. An export, regenerated by catalog.build.export_vocabulary -- do not edit by hand. vocabulary.build applies it over the 148-subject baseline so a rebuild carries every subject added, renamed, redescribed or retired since.

subjects.name: Addiction
subjects.description: Dependence on a substance or behaviour, and attempts to escape it.

subjects.name: Finding Where You Came From
subjects.description: Someone searches for biological family or the truth of their origins.

subjects.name: Selling It
subjects.description: Marketing and persuasion engineered to change what people want.

subjects.name: Getting Older, Facing the End
subjects.description: Ageing, dying and how people prepare for it.

subjects.name: Living With AI
subjects.description: Artificial intelligence entering ordinary life, work or relationships.

subjects.name: What Animals Do
subjects.description: Animal cognition, behaviour and our relationship with other species.

subjects.name: Anthology Framing-Device Fiction
subjects.description: Self-contained episodes unified by a recurring institution or premise, where each episode resolves its own story rather than advancing one continuing mystery — excludes serials with an ongoing plot that carries across episodes.

subjects.name: Killed for Being Queer
subjects.description: Violence directed at people because they are gay, lesbian, bisexual or trans, and the reckoning after — including a police force that declined to look. Not: LGBTQ experience, community and history without violence, which is Queer Lives; not violence because of race, which is Racial Violence; not an organised campaign for equal rights, which is The Fight for Equal Rights.

subjects.name: After the Collapse
subjects.description: Fiction set during or after the breakdown of society.

subjects.name: The Object That Survived
subjects.description: A document, recording or artefact carries a story forward.

subjects.name: Making Art
subjects.description: Artists, their work and the world that receives it.

subjects.name: Artist & Band Biography
subjects.description: The rise, fall or life story of one performer or band, from origins to fame or collapse. Use this when the person is the subject; if the episode is really about how one song or album came to be, that is Song & Album Origin Stories.

subjects.name: The Athlete
subjects.description: An individual competitor's career, talent and pressures.

subjects.name: Scripted Horror
subjects.description: Fiction built to frighten, performed as audio drama.

subjects.name: Scripted Mystery
subjects.description: Fictional investigation, unfolding as scripted drama.

subjects.name: Scripted Science Fiction
subjects.description: Speculative and science-fictional storytelling in scripted audio.

subjects.name: Hired to Break In
subjects.description: Someone breaks into a building, a network or a person's trust with the owner's permission — a red team, a pen test, a social-engineering job, a bug bounty. Nobody is a victim and nobody is pursued. Not: an attack on a target that did not consent, which is Hacked, or one of the four subjects for who did it and why.

subjects.name: The Betting Industry
subjects.description: Legal or illegal betting as a business and what it does to the people and sports around it -- sportsbooks, casinos, lotteries, match-fixing. Not a single gambler's personal ruin, which is addiction-and-recovery.

subjects.name: No Body, No Answer
subjects.description: A death is presumed but the remains are never recovered.

subjects.name: Writers and Books
subjects.description: Authorship, publishing and the life of a text.

subjects.name: Bought Influence
subjects.description: Money changes hands to buy a decision, an admission or a contract.

subjects.name: Buildings & Public Space
subjects.description: A specific building, monument, or public space and the decisions or disputes that shaped its physical form — not the objects inside it or the systems that operate through it.

subjects.name: Two Companies at War
subjects.description: Competitors fight for a market and the contest defines both.

subjects.name: Captivity and Escape
subjects.description: A person is held against their will by kidnappers, hostage-takers, captors, or a prison system, and the story centers on enduring or escaping that confinement; it does NOT cover danger from nature or from an impersonal accident.

subjects.name: The Famous Person
subjects.description: A public figure's life, choices and the shape of their career.

subjects.name: The Charismatic Con
subjects.description: A persuasive individual wins trust and takes money, property or love.

subjects.name: When the Victim Is a Child
subjects.description: A crime against a child and the long reckoning that follows.

subjects.name: Living With Illness
subjects.description: A long-term diagnosis and its effect on daily life and identity.

subjects.name: The Fight for Rights
subjects.description: Organised struggle to win legal and social equality.

subjects.name: A Changing Climate
subjects.description: Warming, its consequences and the effort to slow or adapt to it.

subjects.name: Cold Case Reopened
subjects.description: Dormant evidence or new technology revives an investigation long thought dead.

subjects.name: Spies and the Cold War
subjects.description: Intelligence operations and defections in the long standoff between blocs.

subjects.name: What Empire Left
subjects.description: Colonial rule and the structures it left behind.

subjects.name: A Community Divided
subjects.description: Neighbours split over a decision, a change or an accusation.

subjects.name: The Theory That Spread
subjects.description: A conspiracy belief takes hold and shapes real behaviour.

subjects.name: Corporate Breach and Ransomware Response
subjects.description: Belongs here: a single named organization getting hacked or hit with ransomware, told as an incident timeline of attack, fallout, and recovery; does NOT belong here: the broader criminal marketplace behind an attack or a profile of the attacker's life.

subjects.name: The Company Was Lying
subjects.description: A business misstates what it has built and the deception collapses publicly.

subjects.name: They Knew and Sold It Anyway
subjects.description: A company understood its product or practice caused harm and continued.

subjects.name: Small-Town Power
subjects.description: Local officials or business figures who run a place for themselves.

subjects.name: What Fame Cost
subjects.description: Public attention damages the person receiving it.

subjects.name: Inside the Trial
subjects.description: A prosecution unfolds in court, with strategy, testimony and verdict as the story.

subjects.name: Crypto Gone Wrong
subjects.description: A digital-asset venture implodes, taking investors' holdings with it.

subjects.name: Total Control
subjects.description: A closed group captures members' beliefs, labour or bodies.

subjects.name: Cybercrime for Profit
subjects.description: Belongs here: dark-web markets, carding rings, stolen-data sales, and fraud schemes told from the angle of how the criminal enterprise worked and unraveled; does NOT belong here: a single company's breach response or a biography centered on one hacker's life.

subjects.name: Death in Custody
subjects.description: Someone dies in police or prison hands and accountability is contested.

subjects.name: Facing Execution
subjects.description: A capital sentence and the legal and moral fight around it.

subjects.name: Why It Looks Like That
subjects.description: The design of a building, object or system and the reasoning inside it.

subjects.name: Access and Disability
subjects.description: Disabled people's experience and the barriers built into the world.

subjects.name: Disaster and Accident Survival
subjects.description: A sudden catastrophic event — a shipwreck, fire, mine or cave collapse, crash, or equipment failure — traps or endangers people and sets off an urgent race to rescue them; it does NOT cover a planned expedition into the wild or harm caused deliberately by another person.

subjects.name: Anatomy of a Disaster
subjects.description: Investigators reconstruct exactly how a catastrophe happened.

subjects.name: Early Hacker and Phreaker History
subjects.description: Belongs here: hacking, phone-phreaking, and virus-writing culture from before the commercial internet era, including the first zines, the first viruses, and analog phone-system exploits; does NOT belong here: any breach, malware, or scheme from the post-2000 internet era.

subjects.name: Money and Policy
subjects.description: Interest rates, tax and budget decisions and how they land on ordinary people.

subjects.name: Schools That Failed Them
subjects.description: Educational policy or practice measurably harms the students inside it.

subjects.name: The Vote
subjects.description: Campaigns, elections and the machinery of voting.

subjects.name: The Trusted Employee
subjects.description: A trusted employee — bookkeeper, accountant, office manager — quietly steals from their own employer over months or years, caught only when someone finally adds up the numbers. Not: a company defrauding its customers or investors (The Company Was Lying), and not an outsider running a con on a stranger (The Charismatic Con).

subjects.name: The Thing That Broke
subjects.description: A structure, vehicle or system fails and the design decisions are examined.

subjects.name: Poisoned Ground
subjects.description: Contamination of land, water or air and the community living with it.

subjects.name: Disease at Scale
subjects.description: An outbreak and the public-health response around it.

subjects.name: Broken and Mended Relationships
subjects.description: People separated by conflict attempt, or refuse, repair.

subjects.name: The Small Mystery
subjects.description: An ordinary unexplained thing is chased down for its own sake.

subjects.name: The Engineered Object
subjects.description: A single manufactured object or tool — a steering wheel, a lock, a cassette tape — and the engineering or design choices that made it work, not the building or system it's used inside.

subjects.name: The Movement on the Fringe
subjects.description: An armed or radical political movement, its members and its logic.

subjects.name: Belief and Losing It
subjects.description: Religious conviction, its practice and the crisis of losing it.

subjects.name: Killed Inside the Family
subjects.description: A parent, child, or sibling is the killer, and the crime happens inside the immediate family rather than a marriage. Not: a spouse or dating partner as killer.

subjects.name: The Secret in the Family
subjects.description: A hidden family truth surfaces and changes how relatives see each other.

subjects.name: What We Wear
subjects.description: Garments, style and what clothing signals.

subjects.name: Filmmaker & Star, the Career
subjects.description: One director, actor or producer's working life in film — the pictures they made, how the career rose, turned or ended. Use this when the body of work is the subject; if the episode is really about the private life, marriages or the price of fame, that is The Famous Person or What Fame Cost, and if it is one film's production, that is How It Got Made.

subjects.name: The Old Story
subjects.description: Folk belief, legend and the histories behind them.

subjects.name: Food and How We Eat
subjects.description: Cooking, ingredients, food traditions and the trade around them.

subjects.name: When a Government Falls
subjects.description: A coup, assassination, mass uprising or contested election, and what it did to the people living through it — anywhere in the world. Not a scandal that ended one office-holder's career, which is The Scandal That Broke.

subjects.name: The Evidence Itself
subjects.description: Physical or scientific evidence — DNA, ballistics, a lab result — decides a case.

subjects.name: The Story Nobody Remembers
subjects.description: A significant event that dropped out of public memory is recovered.

subjects.name: Founder & Mogul, the Life
subjects.description: One founder, tycoon or heir and the working life that built, ran or lost a business - including the family that fought over the fortune once the founder was gone. Use this when the person is the subject. If two firms fighting for a market is the story that is Two Companies at War; if it is one firm's grip on a market that is Too Big to Compete With; if it is a company's rise rather than a person's life that is How Big Tech Got Big or The Startup That Fell Apart; and if the person is famous for performing rather than for building, that is The Famous Person.

subjects.name: Friends
subjects.description: Friendship and the obligations inside it.

subjects.name: Games and the People Who Play
subjects.description: Video games, tabletop play and the culture built around them.

subjects.name: Gender and Transition
subjects.description: Gender identity, transition and living outside assigned categories.

subjects.name: A Life Inside the Rules
subjects.description: Someone living inside rules about what their gender may study, wear, marry or become — most often a woman or girl, but a man measured against what a man is supposed to be belongs here too. Told from inside a life. Not: transition or living outside assigned categories, which is Who I Am; not an organised campaign for equal rights, which is The Fight for Equal Rights; not how the category itself was built, which is Where a Category Came From.

subjects.name: Who Gets to Live Here
subjects.description: Housing pressure and displacement reshape a neighbourhood.

subjects.name: The Gossip Business
subjects.description: The business and culture of celebrity gossip journalism itself — columnists, paparazzi, tabloids, who reports on the royals or the stars and why — not a single scandal the press happened to cover.

subjects.name: What the State Hid
subjects.description: Official records or operations kept from the public are brought to light.

subjects.name: Signs, Symbols & Type
subjects.description: A mark, symbol, typeface, flag, language, or visual pattern built to communicate meaning — not a physical object you hold or a building you enter.

subjects.name: Living With Loss
subjects.description: Bereavement and how people carry it afterwards.

subjects.name: Hacker Life Stories
subjects.description: Belongs here: a biography that follows one hacker's path into hacking, their arrest or downfall, and their life after, with the person as the throughline; does NOT belong here: an episode centered on the technical mechanics of one attack or scheme where the perpetrator is just one element.

subjects.name: Breaking Into Systems
subjects.description: Hackers compromise systems, and the pursuit that follows.

subjects.name: The Job
subjects.description: A planned theft and how it was pulled off or came apart — a bank, a vault, a museum, an armoured car. The crime is taking the thing, not hurting someone: a robbery that turns into a killing is a murder story.

subjects.name: History, Retold
subjects.description: A past event or era is rebuilt from the record, revising the accepted account.

subjects.name: Old Hollywood
subjects.description: The film industry's past, its figures and the myths it built.

subjects.name: Without a Home
subjects.description: Housing loss and poverty as lived experience.

subjects.name: An Argument About How to Live
subjects.description: A thinker makes a case about how people should live or what a society owes its members — a lecture, an essay, a long argument with a guest. The episode is the argument, not an event that illustrates one. Not: how a belief spreads through a group, which is Why People Believe It; not a faith held or lost, which is Faith & Doubt.

subjects.name: Living as Someone Else
subjects.description: A person assumes a false identity and sustains it for years.

subjects.name: Starting Over Somewhere Else
subjects.description: Building a life in a new country and what is carried and lost.

subjects.name: Crossing the Border
subjects.description: Migration policy and the lives shaped by enforcement and asylum.

subjects.name: Indigenous Land and Lives
subjects.description: Native and First Nations peoples' history, dispossession and survival.

subjects.name: The Informant
subjects.description: An undercover operative or cooperating witness works inside a target group.

subjects.name: The Institution Closed Ranks
subjects.description: An organisation hides wrongdoing and protects itself over the people it harmed.

subjects.name: How the Internet Behaves
subjects.description: Online communities, virality and the norms that emerge in them.

subjects.name: Killed by a Partner
subjects.description: A spouse or romantic partner is the killer, and the relationship's history — courtship, marriage, the breakup — is the spine of the story. Not: a parent, child, sibling, friend, or neighbour as killer.

subjects.name: Introducing…
subjects.description: A cross-promo: one show's feed carrying the trailer or first episode of a different show. Browsing these is discovery — every one is a doorway to a show you may not know. This is the episode's only label. Not: a show previewing its own next season, which is The Trailer.

subjects.name: Where a Category Came From
subjects.description: How a social category — race, whiteness, masculinity, class — was built, by whom, and what it was built to do. The subject is the construct itself, traced across centuries rather than through one event. Not: violence done to people in its name, which is Racial Violence; not an organised campaign against it, which is The Fight for Equal Rights; not one person living inside it, which is Who I Am or A Woman's Life, Constrained.

subjects.name: How the Reporting Was Done
subjects.description: The reporting itself — the doors knocked, records pulled, dead ends hit.

subjects.name: The Fund That Wasn't
subjects.description: A pooled investment turns out to be a fiction and the money is gone.

subjects.name: The Reporter Who Crossed the Line
subjects.description: A specific journalist or outlet's own conduct — deception, fabrication, or unethical methods used to get a story — becomes the story, not just the coverage they produced. Not: general commentary on how the press covered something.

subjects.name: Children in the System
subjects.description: Young people are processed by courts and detention built for adults.

subjects.name: Taken and Held
subjects.description: A person is abducted and held, and the story turns on their fate.

subjects.name: Workers Organising
subjects.description: Unions, strikes and the fight over who controls work.

subjects.name: Words and Where They Came From
subjects.description: Language, naming and how meaning shifts.

subjects.name: How the Law Actually Works
subjects.description: A lawyer, judge or reporter explains how the legal system works — what a charge means, how bail or sentencing is decided, what a confession is worth. The episode teaches a rule rather than following a case. Not: a specific prosecution, which is A Trial, Start to Finish; not a ruling that changed the law, which is The Case That Changed the Law.

subjects.name: The Case That Changed the Law
subjects.description: A court decision that reshaped what is legal.

subjects.name: A Novel, Performed
subjects.description: Scripted drama adapting a novel or telling a realist story about ordinary lives — no crime to solve, nothing supernatural, no speculative premise. Dickens, Kipling, A Fine Balance. Not: a fictional investigation, which is A Case That Never Happened; not fiction built to frighten, which is Made to Frighten.

subjects.name: How It Got Made
subjects.description: The production story behind a film, show, book or album.

subjects.name: Running Things
subjects.description: How organisations are led, and what good management looks like.

subjects.name: One Attack, Many Victims
subjects.description: One attack on many people at once — a school, a workplace, a public place — and the hours, the survivors, or the fight over what to change afterwards. The weapon does not matter: a shooting, a stabbing, a bombing or a vehicle all belong here. Not: a pattern of separate killings over time, which is The Serial Offender; not an attack whose stated aim is political, which is Terrorism & Its Aftermath.

subjects.name: How the Story Got Told
subjects.description: Journalism and media coverage are themselves examined.

subjects.name: Faking Illness or Cure
subjects.description: Someone fabricates a diagnosis, treatment or recovery for sympathy or profit.

subjects.name: At the Edge of Medicine
subjects.description: New treatments and the research process that produces them.

subjects.name: Harmed by Care
subjects.description: Patients are injured by the very system meant to treat them.

subjects.name: The Mind Under Strain
subjects.description: Mental illness, treatment and how people live with it.

subjects.name: A Person Who Vanished
subjects.description: Someone disappears without explanation and the search consumes those left behind.

subjects.name: Mockumentary Investigation Fiction
subjects.description: Fiction presented as an in-universe investigative podcast, with a host character interviewing sources and narrating a case in real time (e.g. "join the investigation") — excludes shows told through ordinary third-person scripted dialogue with no podcast-host framing.

subjects.name: Too Big to Compete With
subjects.description: A dominant firm's control of a market and its consequences.

subjects.name: Killed by Someone Known
subjects.description: A victim is killed by a spouse, relative or neighbour rather than a stranger.

subjects.name: Paid to Kill
subjects.description: Someone arranges a killing through an intermediary rather than doing it themselves.

subjects.name: The Business Behind the Music
subjects.description: Labels, contracts and money in the music industry.

subjects.name: Music Scene & Movement History
subjects.description: Tells the story of a genre, subculture, nightclub, or defining festival/concert as a collective movement or moment, not the biography of one artist within it.

subjects.name: The Artist Who Died
subjects.description: A musician's death and the story around it.

subjects.name: The Musician Came Apart
subjects.description: A performer's career or life collapses under fame, addiction or crime.

subjects.name: Myth
subjects.description: Traditional myths and the cultures that told them.

subjects.name: When Nature Hit
subjects.description: A storm, fire, flood or quake and how people survived it.

subjects.name: The Bomb and After
subjects.description: Nuclear weapons and power, from development to fallout.

subjects.name: Where the Money Hides
subjects.description: The trade in financial secrecy — shell companies, trusts, tax havens, the lawyers and agents who build them, and the leaks that expose them. The arrangement is usually legal, which is the point. Not: a lie told to investors, which is Investment Fraud; not a company misstating what it built, which is Corporate Fraud; not a regulator failing to act, which is Nobody Was Watching.

subjects.name: Down the Rabbit Hole
subjects.description: Someone is drawn into an extreme worldview through online media.

subjects.name: Organised Crime
subjects.description: A criminal organisation operating as a business — territory, hierarchy and enforcement. The contraband does not matter: drugs, weapons, counterfeits, and the illicit trade in living things — trafficked wildlife, poached rare plants — all belong here.

subjects.name: Scamming as an Industry
subjects.description: Fraud run at industrial scale by an organisation rather than a lone operator.

subjects.name: Investigating the Paranormal
subjects.description: People systematically investigate hauntings or psychic claims.

subjects.name: Raising Children
subjects.description: The practical and emotional work of being a parent.

subjects.name: The Turn
subjects.description: A decision or event redirects the whole course of a life.

subjects.name: Pioneer & Explorer, the Life
subjects.description: One person who went first - explorer, aviator, inventor, nurse, reformer - and the life their firsts cost them. Use this when the person's own record of going first is the subject. If the journey is an ordeal endured rather than a life, that is Staying Alive; if the finding matters more than the finder, that is Figuring It Out; if the flight left the atmosphere, that is Getting to Space; and if the era of invention rather than the inventor is the subject, that is History, Retold.

subjects.name: Police Who Broke the Rules
subjects.description: Officers abuse their power, and the institution around them protects it.

subjects.name: Ruler & Politician, the Life
subjects.description: One person who held or chased political power - monarch, dictator, president, prime minister, revolutionary, courtier - told as a life, from origins through the rise to the rule and the fall. Use this when the person is the subject. If the episode is about what the office can do or a government's decisions rather than the individual who held it, that is The Presidency; if it is one plot, cover-up or downfall rather than a career, that is The Scandal That Broke; if the person is famous for performing rather than for governing, that is The Famous Person.

subjects.name: Punished for Their Politics
subjects.description: The state or an industry punishes private citizens for their beliefs or associations — blacklists, loyalty oaths, naming names, surveillance of dissidents, careers and lives ended by suspicion rather than by a crime. Use this for the machinery of suspicion and its victims; an office-holder brought down by wrongdoing is The Scandal That Broke, and an organised campaign for equal rights is The Fight for Rights. Not Hollywood-specific: the blacklist, McCarthyism, COINTELPRO and their equivalents anywhere belong here.

subjects.name: The Scandal That Broke
subjects.description: A political figure or administration is caught and the fallout reshapes power.

subjects.name: Holding the Office
subjects.description: What the highest office can do and what a leader does with it — the pardon power, emergency powers, a contested transfer, the limits a constitution sets. Any country. Not: the leader's own life story, which is Ruler & Politician, the Life.

subjects.name: Life Inside
subjects.description: Daily existence behind bars, told by people who live or lived it.

subjects.name: Bought and Loaded With Debt
subjects.description: Financial owners extract value from a business or service.

subjects.name: The Power to Charge
subjects.description: Prosecutors' discretion shapes who is punished and how severely.

subjects.name: People in the Street
subjects.description: Mass protest, its organisers and what it did or failed to do.

subjects.name: Why People Believe
subjects.description: How conviction forms and persists against evidence.

subjects.name: Where the Public Money Went
subjects.description: Grants, contracts or relief funds are diverted from their purpose.

subjects.name: Queer Lives
subjects.description: LGBTQ people's experience, community and history.

subjects.name: Racial Violence
subjects.description: Violence directed at people because of race, and the reckoning after.

subjects.name: The Camera Was On
subjects.description: Reality and documentary television and what it does to its subjects.

subjects.name: After Release
subjects.description: Someone rebuilds a life after incarceration and meets the obstacles waiting.

subjects.name: Nobody Was Watching
subjects.description: Oversight meant to prevent harm fails, and the gap is the story.

subjects.name: A Relationship, Remembered
subjects.description: One real relationship, told by the person who lived it — how it began, what strained it, and why it ended, endures, or had to be escaped, including a relationship built on control or fear as seen from inside it. Not general talk about dating or love, and not the criminal case built around it.

subjects.name: Abuse Behind Faith
subjects.description: A religious institution or leader exploits the trust of believers.

subjects.name: Inside the Congregation
subjects.description: Life within a faith community and its teaching.

subjects.name: Bodies and Reproduction
subjects.description: Fertility, pregnancy, abortion and reproductive care.

subjects.name: The Person Online Wasn't Real
subjects.description: An online relationship is built on an invented persona.

subjects.name: Falling In and Out of Love
subjects.description: A relationship's beginning, strain or end.

subjects.name: How Schooling Is Run
subjects.description: A decision about how schools operate — a curriculum, a phone ban, a new kind of school, a reading programme that worked — told without a claim of harm. Not: policy or practice that measurably damages the students inside it, which is When School Fails a Child.

subjects.name: Figuring It Out
subjects.description: A scientific question is pursued and something is learned.

subjects.name: Who Got to Be on Screen
subjects.description: Which people the movies let on screen and what they were allowed to play — the roles offered to Black, Asian, queer and women performers, the stereotypes written for them, and how those conventions changed. Use this when the pattern across films is the subject; a single performer's career is Filmmaker & Star, the Career, and the contracts and censors behind it are The Studio System.

subjects.name: Scripted Survival Drama
subjects.description: A fictional, scripted audio drama built around a survival premise (post-apocalyptic, horror, monster-infested outposts) performed by actors in serialized chapters; it does NOT cover a real person's first-person account of what happened to them.

subjects.name: This Particular Place
subjects.description: A town, region or landscape and the character of life there.

subjects.name: The Serial Offender
subjects.description: One person commits a pattern of violent crimes across many victims.

subjects.name: Sex, Work and Coercion
subjects.description: Sex work, trafficking and the line between choice and coercion.

subjects.name: Sexual Abuse and Accountability
subjects.description: Sexual violence or exploitation and the long fight to hold someone answerable.

subjects.name: Slavery and What Followed
subjects.description: The institution of slavery and how its consequences persist.

subjects.name: Song & Album Origin Stories
subjects.description: How one specific song or album was written, recorded or became famous — the room, the take, the argument over the mix. Use this when the work is the subject; a career retold through its hits is Artist & Band Biography.

subjects.name: How the Song Was Made
subjects.description: A musician breaks down the construction of a specific piece of music.

subjects.name: Getting to Space
subjects.description: Spaceflight missions, the engineering behind them and the people who flew.

subjects.name: Sport as Politics
subjects.description: Athletic competition becomes a stage for political conflict.

subjects.name: The Game That Mattered
subjects.description: A defining game, season or era in a sport.

subjects.name: Cheating and Cover-Ups in Sport
subjects.description: Doping, fixing or institutional wrongdoing inside a sport.

subjects.name: The Startup That Fell Apart
subjects.description: A venture built on hype or bad decisions comes undone.

subjects.name: State-Sponsored Cyber Espionage
subjects.description: Belongs here: hacking, spyware, or malware directed or backed by a national government, military, or intelligence agency for espionage, sabotage, or geopolitical leverage; does NOT belong here: hacking carried out by independent criminals or hobbyists chasing money or fame.

subjects.name: Killed by a Stranger
subjects.description: One killing where the victim and the killer had no relationship before it, and the case was answered. Not: a partner, relative or neighbour as killer; not a pattern across victims; not a contract killing; not a case still open.

subjects.name: The Studio System
subjects.description: How the film industry actually ran as a business — studio contracts and moguls, the Production Code and the ratings that replaced it, publicity machinery, star grooming, unions, box office and who got paid. Use this when an institution or era of the business is the subject, not a person's career and not the making of one film.

subjects.name: Something Not Explainable
subjects.description: A first-person account of an event with no natural explanation.

subjects.name: Surreal Narrator Speculative Serial
subjects.description: Fiction carried by a single first-person narrator or monologue through a dreamlike or dystopian world, where atmosphere and voice drive the episode rather than a case being solved — excludes multi-character dialogue-driven mystery plots.

subjects.name: Being Watched
subjects.description: Monitoring by states or companies and its effect on ordinary life.

subjects.name: Staying Alive
subjects.description: A person endures an extreme situation against long odds.

subjects.name: Invisible Systems
subjects.description: A process, protocol, or network — an ambulance dispatch system, a hospital workflow, a GPS network — whose design shapes outcomes at scale, not a single object or building.

subjects.name: Talking About the Movies
subjects.description: Hosts talk about films as films — a recommendation run, a ranking, a rewatch, listener mail, one old picture appreciated. The pleasure is the conversation, not a story being told. Not: a career, which is Filmmaker & Star, the Career; not one film's production, which is How It Got Made; not the industry's past, which is Old Hollywood.

subjects.name: Talking About Love
subjects.description: A host and a guest work through a pattern in relationships — jealousy, trust, dating, monogamy — as a general conversation, not one person's own story and not a memoir of one specific relationship.

subjects.name: Talking About the Music
subjects.description: Hosts talk about music as music — a chart round-up, a trivia round, listener mail, a recap of the main series. The pleasure is the conversation. Not: a genre or scene and the moment it mattered, which is The Scene & Its Moment; not one song's making, which is Song & Album Origin Stories; not a performer's life, which is The Rise and Fall.

subjects.name: How Big Tech Got Big
subjects.description: A technology company's rise and the power it accumulated.

subjects.name: The Attack and After
subjects.description: A terrorist act and the political and personal changes it forces.

subjects.name: The Trailer
subjects.description: A show's own preview of itself or a coming season — a taste of the thing, not the thing. This is the episode's only label: a trailer is not about its show's subject, it is an advertisement for it. Not: a preview of a different show, which is Introducing…

subjects.name: How Things Move
subjects.description: Roads, rail, shipping and the built systems people depend on.

subjects.name: True Crime About True Crime
subjects.description: The true-crime genre's ethics, audience and effects examined.

subjects.name: Undercover for the Story
subjects.description: The reporter goes undercover, embeds with the subject, or otherwise puts themselves at personal risk to get the story — the danger to the reporter is part of the story, not just the byline. Not: standard records-and-interviews reporting done at a safe remove.

subjects.name: Unsolved Murder
subjects.description: A killing that was never solved, revisited years later for new leads.

subjects.name: Nobody Went Looking
subjects.description: Police or the state dismissed, delayed, or mishandled the search itself, and the story indicts that response as much as the disappearance — most often an Indigenous woman, a marginalised community, or a journalist in a conflict zone. Not: a case where the search was taken seriously and simply failed.

subjects.name: The One Who Chose to Vanish
subjects.description: The missing person chose to disappear — faking death, fleeing debt, or walking away from their old life — rather than being taken or harmed against their will. Not: a disappearance later revealed to be murder or abduction.

subjects.name: How the War Was Fought
subjects.description: Military campaigns, the decisions behind them and their human cost.

subjects.name: Answering for War
subjects.description: Atrocities committed in wartime and attempts to hold someone responsible.

subjects.name: The Person Who Spoke Up
subjects.description: An insider reports wrongdoing and bears the consequences.

subjects.name: Wilderness Expedition Survival
subjects.description: A person or group who chose to be in a remote natural setting — mountain, polar ice, jungle, or open-sea voyage — must survive nature itself (weather, terrain, isolation, distance from help); it does NOT cover a sudden accident, mechanical failure, or someone else's captors as the threat.

subjects.name: The Conditions of the Job
subjects.description: What a job actually demands of the people doing it.

subjects.name: Convicted of the Wrong Crime
subjects.description: Someone is imprisoned for an act the evidence does not support.

retired.reason: Same definition space as The Scene & Its Moment (music-scene-movement), same theme. Two labelling agents reported they could not tell them apart, and one named the consequence: two agents labelling the same episode differently would register as disagreement rather than as the vocabulary fault it is. Kept the one whose definition names what it excludes. The 638 rows on this slug belong to the 2026-07-theming run and are untouched.
